title.narrative: Protection and Response for Vulnerable Populations in Crisis-affected Regions of Northwest, Southwest and Far North Region of Cameroon

description.narrative: The CERF UFE-funded project has two components, a sector-specific and the climate envelope. The objective of the CERF UFE sector specific is to deliver life-saving protection and assistance, including shelter/NFI responses, to forcibly displaced individuals—internally displaced persons, refugees, returnees—and vulnerable host communities in the Far North, North-West, and South-West (NWSW) regions. For nearly a decade, these populations have been severely affected by humanitarian crises that have deepened their vulnerabilities, including attacks by non-state armed groups, intercommunal violence, and seasonal climate shocks. UNHCR’s protection response aims to strengthen community-based protection committees to reinforce community efforts in preventing and reducing human rights violations, including mitigating Gender-Based Violence risks. Finally, it seeks to enhance response efforts through community participation and the empowerment of targeted localities. These interventions align with the two strategic priorities outlined in the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for Cameroon 2022-2026, the Sustainable Development Goals 1,2,3,6, 9,10,11, 13, 15, 16, and 17, and the Cameroon National Development Strategy 2030. Through this funding, UNHCR intends to strengthen the protection of forcibly displaced persons and host communities by enhancing their access to quality basic social services in a sustainable manner. Specifically, the following activities will be implemented:(i) Protection Monitoring and Response, including data collection and analysis of human rights violations, reinforcing the protection capacity of community-based committees and managing GBV cases, including providing psychosocial support to victims of human rights violations and referral services targeting 12,500 IDPs, returnees, refugees, and host communities. (ii) Shelter and NFI provision to 16,800 forcibly displaced and vulnerable persons through a mixed modality approach.(iii) Multipurpose Cash for Protection Response to 910 persons with specific needs and the most vulnerable affected populations. For shelter and NFI responses, in addition to cash-based interventions (CBI) for shelter and NFIs, cash for rent will be provided to vulnerable IDPs in urban and peri-urban areas where rental facilities are available and accessible.The Climate Envelope component aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by integrating renewable energy solutions into water production systems, such as solar-powered water pumps and energy-efficient water treatment facilities, which lowers emissions and ensures a sustainable water supply. It also seeks to enhance the resilience of refugees and local host populations to climate impacts by developing climate-resilient infrastructure, and improving drainage systems, thereby reducing vulnerability to flooding. This intervention aligns with the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), the Kyoto Convention, and the Paris Climate Agreement.(i) Key activities include installing solar-powered water pumps, promoting water-efficient irrigation techniques, constructing drainage infrastructure and upgrading WASH facilities in Minawao Camp.(ii) The targeted populations are 6,000 refugees in Minawao Camp and surrounding host communities. They will benefit from improved WASH facilities, and renewable energy solutions. These efforts contribute to building climate resilience by reducing vulnerability, enhancing adaptive capacity, promoting sustainable development, fostering community engagement, and improving ecosystem health.
